pr_title: release-21.2: opt: do not add invalid casts to match types in set operations
pr_body:
Backport 1/1 commits from #75219 on behalf of @mgartner.

/cc @cockroachdb/release

----

The optbuilder adds casts in order to match non-identical left/right
types of set operations like UNION (see #60560). This change prevents
the optbuilder from adding casts that are invalid, which caused internal
errors. Now, a user error is thrown if no such cast exists from the left
or right input type to the output type.

Fixes #70831

Release note (bug fix): A bug has been fixed that caused internal errors
in queries with set operations, like UNION, when corresponding columns
on either side of the set operation were not the same. This error only
occurred with a limited set of types. This bug is present in versions
20.2.6+, 21.1.0+, and 21.2.0+.

----

Release justification: This fixes a rare bug that causes internal errors.

issue_context.title: opt: internal error because optbuilder `addCasts` adds a `tuple[]` cast that we don't support
issue_context.body:
This is spun off to track a failure causing https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/70663 https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/70669 https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/70667 https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/70666 and https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/70670

The error `internal error: no volatility for cast tuple[]::tuple{bool, unknown}[]` is returned when running this query.

```
SELECT * FROM (VALUES (ARRAY[(true, NULL)])) AS v1
  EXCEPT ALL SELECT * FROM (VALUES (ARRAY[]::RECORD[])) AS v2;
```

Using `bisect` I found that the bug was introduced in 4037bd8 which made it into v21.1.0 and was also backported to v20.2 (#61086). This commit seems to modify `addCasts` in optbuilder/union.go in a way that causes it to add casts that we don't actually support.

cc @mgartner and @yuzefovich who were tagged on the above issues.
comments:
I don't yet have a full understanding of how set operations are supposed to work with tuple types (records). Postgres prevents comparison operators between tuples with a different number of elements and tuples element types that do not have implicit casts to each other (this is what I would expect):

```
marcus=# select row(1, 2) > row(1);
ERROR:  42601: unequal number of entries in row expressions

marcus=# select row(1, 2) > row(3, true);
ERROR:  42883: operator does not exist: integer > boolean
```

But it is odd to me that Postgres disallows set operations when columns have different types, but allows set operations when columns have tuple types with a different number of elements or element types:

```
marcus=# select 1 union all select true;
ERROR:  42804: UNION types integer and boolean cannot be matched

marcus=# select row(1) union all select row(1, 2);
  row
-------
 (1)
 (1,2)
(2 rows)

marcus=# select row(1) union all select row(true);
 row
-----
 (1)
 (t)
(2 rows)
```

One thing that I've noticed from working on tuple support recently is that Postgres is lax about tuple types in some contexts. Consider also that Postgres is fine with arrays of mismatched tuple types:

```
rafiss@127:postgres> select array[row(1,2),row(1,2,3), row(1,2,'cat'), null]
+--------------------------------------+
| array                                |
|--------------------------------------|
| {"(1,2)","(1,2,3)","(1,2,cat)",NULL} |
+--------------------------------------+
```

But if you try to use it in different ways, it may or may not error at execution time depending on what needs to be evaluated:
```
rafiss@127:postgres> select array_position(array[row(1,2,1),row(1,2,3), row(1,2,'cat'), null], row(1,2,5))
cannot compare dissimilar column types integer and unknown at record column 3

rafiss@127:postgres> select array_position(array[row(1,2),row(1,2,3), row(1,2,'cat'), null], row(1,2,5))
cannot compare record types with different numbers of columns

rafiss@127:postgres> select array_position(array[row(1,2),row(1,2,3), row(1,2,'cat'), null], row(1,3))
+------------------+
| array_position   |
|------------------|
| <null>           |
+------------------+

rafiss@127:postgres> select array_position(array[row(1,2),row(1,2,3), row(1,2,'cat'), null], row(1,2))
+------------------+
| array_position   |
|------------------|
| 1                |
+------------------+
```

review_comments: i noticed that this test case differs from the one in #75219 - is that on purpose?

Yes. In #75219 we're using the OID->OID `castMap` to determine which casts are valid. In the backports `castMap` does not yet exist, so we're using the family->family `validCasts`. They don't match up perfectly so the cast from `types.Any` -> `types.Bool` that is not allowed on master is allowed in these release branches, so the test had to change.
